intended_use: Vessel-specific system-level research baselines covering dynamic energy, lifecycle GHG, cost and cargo/storage trade-offs. Values are study outcomes, not universal fuel properties or independent certification of a commercial product.
comparison_policy: Keep each source tied to its actual vessel, route, operational profile, geography, technology assumptions and functional unit.
Do not combine the container-ship study and the 6177-GT general-cargo study into one ranking.
Report upstream fuel production, onboard processing, tank-to-wake, components, replacements, cargo payload, route and lifecycle boundaries separately.
PEMFC stack efficiency is not the same as whole-plant propulsion efficiency; include reforming/cracking, balance of plant, power electronics and auxiliaries.
Tank volume and cargo deadweight penalties are vessel-specific and must not be transferred as universal multipliers.
The article's interpretation of adopted/projected IMO GFI trajectories is a study result; verify legal/regulatory status against the current official IMO instrument before any compliance claim.
Null values and missing uncertainty remain unknown, not zero.

sources.title: Comparative multi-criteria assessment of electro-fuel-based marine power systems for container ships
sources.data_availability: Supplementary data and detailed model inputs stated as available on request in the article.
sources.method_summary: High-fidelity dynamic energy modelling, lifecycle environmental assessment, techno-economic analysis, IMO-related GFI/EEXI assessment, TOPSIS multi-criteria decision analysis and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis (1000 Latin-hypercube samples).

sources.title: Environmental and economic assessment of alternative marine energy pathways using integrated life cycle analysis
sources.method_summary: Well-to-wake life-cycle assessment with GREET and OpenLCA / Environmental Footprint 3.0, life-cycle cost assessment over vessel service life and 10000-iteration Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. Uses real operational data from a 6177-GT general-cargo vessel in the Mediterranean and Black Sea.

Fuel cost, electrolytic production pathway, onboard processing, PEMFC stack life and capital costs strongly affect rankings.

limitations: One 6177-GT vessel and two regional seas; no direct transfer to deep-sea container or inland vessel design.
The 3.7× tank volume and 6.8% cargo displacement are vessel-specific and distinct from the RSC 2026 container-ship tank-energy-density ratios.
E-fuel GHG performance depends on the upstream electricity, hydrogen, carbon and feedstock pathways used in the study.
Full model inputs and route data must be obtained before independent reproduction.

design_implications: Fuel choice is inseparable from conversion topology, onboard processing and ship-specific operating profiles.
A direct-hydrogen PEMFC result cannot be attributed to ammonia- or methanol-fed PEMFC systems without including cracker/reformer energy and balance-of-plant parasitics.
Economic and climate-optimal configurations can differ even on the same vessel and study assumptions.
A 6177-GT general-cargo vessel result must not be combined with a deep-sea container-ship result as if both share hull, route and load conditions.
Tank-volume and cargo displacement must be measured against each study's vessel geometry and reserve policy.
